sections.heading: The exemption still requires a notice
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 section 559.802 conditions the exemption from Part VII on a franchise meeting the federal definition, a notice stating substantial compliance with applicable Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requirements, and payment of the set fee before the covered offer or sale.

sections.heading: Separate the worker’s covenant from the operator’s agreement
paragraphs: The reviewed 2026 section 8-2-113 addresses restrictions on an individual’s compensation for labour. The employer, worker, work location and actual restriction matter; an entity-level brand agreement is a different question.

Exceptions have conditions involving compensation, trade secrets, extent of restriction and other defined categories. Separate confidentiality, customer restrictions and noncompetition by their actual conduct, duration, area and protected interest. A confidentiality heading does not establish a noncompete exception.

The 2026 PAY CALC Order, effective February 1, 2026, lists $130,014 annually for highly compensated employees. Section 8-2-113 defines the covenant threshold as the greater of the Division’s August 10, 2022 amount or the amount when the covenant is executed; do not use a later year’s number automatically for an older agreement. For the stated noncompete exception, annualized cash compensation must meet the applicable threshold both when entered and enforced, the covenant must protect trade secrets and be no broader than reasonably necessary. The customer-nonsolicitation branch uses sixty percent of that threshold and its own trade-secret/narrowness conditions. Both branches exclude the stated restrictions on medicine, advanced-practice registered nursing and dentistry. Compensation alone is not eligibility.

sections.heading: Notice is required only for an otherwise permissible covered covenant
paragraphs: A prospective worker must receive the required notice and terms before accepting employment. A current worker must receive them at least fourteen days before the earlier of the covenant’s effective date or the effective date of additional compensation or employment-term changes providing consideration for it.
The notice must be clear and conspicuous, signed and in a separate document with the required language. Correct notice does not validate an otherwise impermissible restriction.

The notice must accompany a copy of the agreement, identify it by name and warn that it contains a restriction on later employment, and point to the specific sections. Its language must be the language used about the worker’s performance. These form requirements do not validate an otherwise void restriction.

sections.heading: Submit the right package for the actual seller
paragraphs: Hawaii’s Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs (DCCA) directs franchise filings to the Securities Online Portal. Its tips call for the required materials together under the relevant initial, renewal or amendment category, with the associated fee.

sections.heading: Test the buyback or income promise separately
paragraphs: RS 51:1821 puts registered-mark wording within the specified sales/marketing-plan branch. Specified device-location help, product buyback and earnings/refund representations have separate conditions. Device placement is not every form of customer-finding or site advice.

For example, a German seller promising to buy back output if the operator is dissatisfied must test that promise separately from its registered mark. The actual payments and other conditions still matter.

sections.heading: When the bond requirement applies
paragraphs: RS 51:1822 requires covered bonds before conducting business, including advertising or soliciting. Subsections A and B require authorized-surety bond face amounts of $50,000 for a covered seller and $25,000 for a covered agent, including the stated independent contractor, broker or employee roles. These are bond amounts, not a quoted premium or application fee; the actual role matters. Subsection G limits the bond duty to opportunities defined in 1821(1)(a), (b) or (c), not every trademark licence.

For those opportunities, subsection H makes the bond continuous. The surety—the company guaranteeing the bond—can terminate through 60 days’ written notice to the specified assistant secretary and the principal, whose obligations the bond guarantees; liability continues during that period and for accrued pre-termination liability discovered later. Subsection E requires a new/additional bond before continuing business. The 60 days is a bond rule, not franchise-contract exit notice.

sections.heading: The agreement must reflect covered oral promises
paragraphs: For covered opportunities, RS 51:1823 addresses documented earnings support, specified ad disclosures, actual seller identification and appointment of the secretary of state for service of process.

Subsection (6) requires the written agreement to include material oral statements, representations and promises made before execution. Subsection (7) prohibits waiver of purchaser legal rights; signing does not erase the earlier sales conversation.

sections.heading: A separate rule applies to real-estate brokerage
paragraphs: RS 37:1465 prohibits the described franchisor from contracting with a Louisiana real-estate broker without appointing a Louisiana-licensed broker as state representative. Property maintenance is not automatically brokerage.

Bond amounts are not premiums or a general service-franchise duty.

proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: A New Jersey office-based distributor can fall within the Franchise Practices Act, but office activity alone is not enough. Establish the written brand/community-of-interest relationship and the applicable combined criteria.

sections.heading: The Act has its own relationship definition
paragraphs: Section 56:10-3 requires the stated written arrangement for a definite or indefinite period, permission to use a trade name/mark/service mark or related characteristics, and a community of interest—the parties’ shared commercial interest—in marketing goods or services. A distribution label does not decide those facts.

For the place-of-business test, an office or warehouse is generally excluded. But for persons without a majority of sales directly to consumers, qualifying offices/warehouses from which personnel visit/call customers or goods are delivered can count. An address alone is insufficient.

sections.heading: For the general route, all three application criteria matter
paragraphs: Section 56:10-4(a) requires the following together for the franchisee, the operator receiving the rights. Section 4(b) has a separate new-motor-vehicle franchise route, not the same three-test rule.

rows: Performance contemplates or requires the franchisee to establish/maintain the defined location.
Covered product/service gross sales exceeded $35,000 during the twelve months immediately before suit is instituted.
More than 20% of the franchisee’s gross sales are intended to be or derived from the franchise.

sections.heading: Coverage is not a ruling on this operator
paragraphs: Section 56:10-8 excludes a franchise granted before the Act’s effective date, while renewal or amendment is not excluded on that basis. The source gives December 21, 1971 as the Act’s effective date.
